profile.name: Shreyaan Vashishtha
profile.title: BEng Mechanical Engineering @ HKUST | Astrix Team Member | Peer Mentor
profile.tagline: Mechanical Engineering undergraduate at HKUST with a strong foundation in mechanical design, rapid prototyping, and physics-based problem solving. Currently engineering Project Aquanaut (underwater submersible) and previously Astrix Rocketry Aerodynamics & Descent Control.

status.text: BEng Mechanical Engineering @ HKUST • Astrix Project Aquanaut

bio: Mechanical Engineering undergraduate at HKUST with a strong foundation in mechanical design, rapid prototyping, and physics-based problem solving.
Currently an engineer on the Astrix team working on Project Aquanaut, focusing on 3D CAD modeling and structural hull design for a custom underwater submersible.
Previously contributed to aerodynamic packaging and recovery systems for the Descent & Payload rocketry team, as well as UAV airframe R&D prototyping at ZeroDrag.

projects.title: Project Aquanaut — Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
projects.description: Structural hull architecture, multi-quadrant additive manufacturing, and watertight electronics enclosure for an autonomous, GPS-navigated semi-submersible vehicle.
projects.longDescription:
• Engineered the structural hull architecture for an autonomous, GPS-navigated semi-submersible vehicle using Autodesk Fusion 360 and SolidWorks, selecting a rectangular shell design to maximize roll stability and optimize the rotational moment arm for the thruster configuration.

• Subdivided the primary external shell into 12 distinct sections for optimized additive manufacturing, prototyping the multi-quadrant enclosure using PETG filament to evaluate structural tolerances prior to final integration.

• Designed a cost-effective, accessible core watertight enclosure to safely house the PCB, embedded firmware, and battery, ensuring environmental sealing against water ingress while maintaining accessibility for on-deck debugging.

• Co-led cross-functional team structuring for an 8-member engineering project at Astrix, working to accelerate the transition from conceptual ideas to a deployable prototype.

projects.title: Flight & Recovery Systems (Aerodynamic & Descent Control)
projects.description: Flight and recovery mechanisms for the CanSat competition, optimizing aerodynamic stability, parachute/paraglider deployment dynamics, and descent rates.
projects.longDescription:
• Engineered flight and recovery mechanisms for the CanSat competition, focusing on the reliable deployment and safe descent of aerospace systems.

• Designed and iterated on mechanical components to optimize aerodynamic stability and descent control parameters, including parachute and paraglider deployments.

• Prototyped structural mechanisms using CAD software (SolidWorks) and integrated them into the broader vehicle architecture.

• Tested various configurations of the deployment of parachute and paraglider, measuring descent rates and verifying performance against competition guidelines.

• Collaborated within a multidisciplinary student engineering team at Astrix to meet overall vehicle and payload design requirements.

projects.title: ZeroDrag — UAV Drone Frame Design & Rapid Prototyping
projects.description: Precision CAD modeling, 3D printing, and rapid prototype testing of UAV drone frames and related aerodynamic components during R&D engineering internship.
projects.longDescription:
• Designed and optimized UAV drone frames and related aerodynamic components using CAD (Autodesk Fusion 360) at ZeroDrag in Noida, India.

• Developed and bench-tested 3D-printed prototypes through rapid iteration, converting design concepts into functional hardware.

• Identified design issues, vibration profiles, and stress points to refine structural components based on real-world flight test results.

• Gained hands-on experience across the entire product development cycle: CAD modeling, rapid prototyping, structural iteration, and flight testing.

projects.title: High-Tolerance CAD & Precision Mechanisms
projects.description: Multi-body assemblies with GD&T tolerances, interactive WebGL 3D visualizations, and rapid additive prototyping in SolidWorks and Fusion 360.
projects.longDescription:
• Engineered multi-body assemblies with GD&T tolerances, rapid prototyping via FDM/SLA 3D printing, and structural stress validation.

• Integrated with interactive browser-based Three.js WebGL inspection engine allowing real-time orbit, wireframe topology inspection, and engineering orthographic view snapping.

• Features aerospace avionics modules, supersonic fin cans, dual-axis sensor gimbals, and structural chassis designs.
